column3: Close to the Greek. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB has “God the Father” without “our,” following manuscripts that lack it.
NASB renders “is increasing exceedingly” as “is greatly enlarged” and “is abounding” as “grows ever greater.”
NASB follows the critical text (“boast”); it renders “boast” as “speak proudly” and “tribulations” as “afflictions.”
NASB renders “a plain token” as “a plain indication” and “be accounted worthy” as “be considered worthy.”
NASB adds “after all” and “only” and renders “those oppressing you” as “those who afflict you.”
NASB adds “to give” and “as well,” renders “repose” as “relief,” and moves “in flaming fire,” which opens v. 8 in the Greek, into this verse.
NASB begins after the phrase moved to v. 7; it follows the critical text without “Christ” and renders “inflicting vengeance” as “dealing out retribution.”
NASB renders “will suffer the penalty” as “will pay the penalty.”
NASB follows the critical text; it moves “on that day” forward and sets the last clause off with a dash.
NASB renders “every good pleasure of goodness” as “every desire for goodness” and adds “your.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Christ” in the first phrase.
